$comment: The CLOSED set of UNIVERSAL FACILITIES this repository may publish.
`release-facility.yml` resolves its target here through
`scripts/release_facility.py resolve` and fails closed, so adding a
publishable facility is a reviewed diff rather than a dispatch-time
string — the same doctrine as `.github/release-modules.json` and
`.github/release-adapters.json`, applied to a third shape.
## Why this is a THIRD file rather than a row in one of the other two
A universal facility (ADR-0070; see `packages/dotmac-deployment-
foundation/EXTRACTION.toml`'s `classification`) has no `ModuleManifest`,
no `mod_*` namespace and no migration lineage — so a reader sent to
`.github/release-modules.json` to add one would be looking for three
facts (`db_schema`, `manifest_attr`, `kernel_floor`) that do not exist,
exactly as `.github/release-adapters.json` already explains for a
stateless protocol adapter.
It is not an adapter either, and that is the half worth spelling out. An
adapter is CALLED FROM a product's own process — a product imports it, so
its release proof is an IMPORT-SURFACE proof: every `__all__` name
resolves against the installed bytes. A universal facility is a BUILD-TIME
tool a product's CI shells out to; nothing imports
`dotmac_deployment_foundation` at request time, and the package declares
zero runtime dependencies precisely so it never could. Its release proof
is therefore that its CONSOLE SCRIPT (`dotmac-deploy`) runs against a real
descriptor — `scripts/release_facility.py`'s docstring calls this out:
'an importable module proves nothing about a console script'. Folding a
facility into `release-adapters.json` would mean either weakening
`verify-wheel`'s `__all__` proof to accommodate a package with no reason
to be imported, or leaving a CLI entry point that could be silently
broken (a missing `console_scripts` line, a typo'd target) while the
import-surface check passed anyway.
## The classification is checked, not trusted
`resolve` reads the package's `EXTRACTION.toml` and refuses anything
whose `classification` is not `universal-facility`. That is what stops
this lane from becoming a way to publish a module or an adapter while
skipping the checks their own classification requires.
## Why it is populated, unlike `release-adapters.json` was at first
`.github/release-adapters.json` stayed empty until a real pilot consumer
ran the ceremony end to end — absence was the safety mechanism there,
because an adapter's whole risk is a product trusting a security-bearing
surface nobody had exercised. A universal facility carries none of that
risk profile: it decides no business fact and holds no rows
(`EXTRACTION.toml`'s `shadow_and_drift`), and its own dossier's
`next_action` names 'a first release through the release lane this
package is enrolled in' as the very next, unblocked step — not gated on
a pilot consumer the way the OIDC adapter was. Before this file existed
no release lane in this repository accepted a `universal-facility`
classification at all, so `dotmac-deployment-foundation` could not be
published and every CI job installing it from the index was gated shut
by construction. Listing it now is the fix for that circularity, not a
relaxation of the doctrine: publication is still not adoption —
`EXTRACTION.toml`'s `contract_consumers` stays empty and a release moves
it not at all.
The one build- and deploy-time facility every Dotmac product
assembly composes (ADR-0070).
NO db_schema, manifest_attr or kernel_floor, and their absence is
checked rather than assumed: scripts/release_facility.py refuses an
entry carrying any of them. This package has no ModuleManifest, no
lineage and no ledger allocation, and it depends on nothing at
runtime — not dotmac-kernel, not SQLAlchemy, not FastAPI, not
Jinja, not a YAML library.
Required wheel contents, each earning its place rather than
listing the directory:
cli.py            -- dotmac-deploy, the surface this lane proves
execution_bindings.py + discovery.py -- what makes the installed CLI
able to ADMIT at all. Without them `--execute` can
only ever refuse: there is no way for an assembly
to supply an AuthorizationVerifier or an effects
provider, which is precisely the a4 defect that
made that candidate unpublishable. A wheel missing
them passes every import check and cannot deploy
anything.
application_profile.py -- ApplicationFoundationProfile.v1. `cli.py`
imports it on the deploy path to carry the profile
digest into the execution plan, so absent from the
wheel every `deploy` raises ImportError.
spec.py           -- ProductDeploymentSpec.v1 and its refusals
conformance.py    -- the checks a consuming product runs in its
own CI (deployment-conformance.yml calls it)
errors.py         -- the taxonomy the CLI's exit codes rely on
secrets_guard.py  -- ADR-0009: names and pointers, never values
execution_plan.py -- FoundationExecutionPlanV1 and
ExecutionPlanDigestV1. Two OTHER repositories
bind to its canonicalization: Platform CP
submits the digest and Control freezes it, so a
wheel without this module leaves them unable to
produce the value at all
recovery_execution.py -- the restore EXECUTOR the installed CLI drives
through `restore-rehearsal --execute`. Absent from
the wheel, that subcommand raises ImportError at the
moment an operator runs it, which is the failure this
list exists to make impossible
external_recovery.py + recovery_identity.py -- the signed
RecoveryReceipt.v1 contract and the typed
executor/dataset identities it compares. Without
them a descriptor declaring an external executor
does not parse and the GATE step has no handler,
so the deployment fails at plan build rather
than merely lacking a feature
engine/plan.py    -- the ordered deployment plan as data
image/audit.py    -- the hardened OCI image contract
render/compose.py -- the deterministic Compose renderer
render/nginx.py   -- the deterministic ingress renderer
A wheel missing any of them is not a smaller facility; it is one
whose CLI cannot do what its README promises.
allowed_requires is empty: the package's own pyproject.toml names
no runtime dependency beyond the Python version itself, so any
Requires-Dist line at all is a defect, not a closure to review.
Publication is not adoption. EXTRACTION.toml's status stays
audit-complete and contract_consumers stays empty until a real
product cutover (first_cutover names dotmac_erp) merges against the
published wheel; a release moves neither.
